dedupe_keys.name: how is ict use linked to household transport expenditure a cross national macro analysis of the influence of home broadband access

description: Myriam Bris, Jacek Pawlak and John Polak at Imperial College London publish a cross-country table linking transport expenditure and home Internet access. The Zenodo CSV is free under CC BY-NC 4.0. Coverage is a 2010 cross-section of thirty-three countries, with average household transport spending, broadband access and macroeconomic or infrastructure controls. These observations can calibrate aggregate travel-demand scenarios that represent interactions with digital access. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this table. A second Zenodo deposit exposes the same filename, size and MD5 checksum and is treated as a duplicate. The paper estimates an association using a log-log model and instrumental-variable checks, but a single cross-section cannot establish how any particular household changes travel after obtaining broadband. Country coverage, spending-unit comparability and missing values were not checked in the CSV. No data were downloaded or regression reproduced, and present-day transfer requires new evidence.
